text:
debora_l: Quick sync  I added a small how-to + example CSV export and reconciliation snippet for quota migrations. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4021. This came from support tickets where customers needed to reconcile legacy quota usage after tier cutovers.

viv_ansari: nice. can you summarize what the CSV contains? that helps reviewers.

debora_l: sure  the CSV example has columns: request_ts, route, model, tokens_consumed, quota_attribute, x_request_id. I included a short note on rounding rules for embedding units.

ton y_k: tiny nit: our ingestion pipeline maps quota_attribute -> tenant_id, and some legacy logs used "quota_tier" header. docs should show both and recommend normalizing.

debora_l: added normalization example and a Go snippet that normalizes headers when parsing CSVs.

```go
// normalize headers example (illustrative)
func normalizeQuotaAttr(h string) string {
  switch strings.ToLower(h) {
  case "x-redwood-quota-tenant", "quota_tier":
    return "tenant_id"
  default:
    return h
  }
}
```

viv_ansari: love the Go example. can we also show a tiny SQL query to aggregate tokens by tenant for a given day? support often asks for that.

debora_l: added a short SQL sample: 

```sql
SELECT tenant_id, SUM(tokens_consumed) AS tokens
FROM usage_exports
WHERE DATE(request_ts) = '2026-02-15'
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY tokens DESC;
```

ton y_k: we should also call out timing caveats: when a tier change happens, exports may contain mixed-attribution rows during the migration window. added a 2-line FAQ entry.

debora_l: done. i also linked to the billing migration playbook and recommended including x-request-id and exact timestamps when filing support tickets.

infra-bot: lint: code fence languages missing for one block.

debora_l: fixed all code fences, pushed.

product-bot: reminder: please mark this doc as "operational" if it contains internal reconciliation steps.

debora_l: flagged as operational and moved the reconciliation appendix to an internal-only include; public doc keeps CSV schema, Go and SQL examples, and a short section on producing a public snapshot showing quota attribution changes over time.

viv_ansari: approved, small editorial nit on wording of rounding rules.

debora_l: addressed, thanks! merging after CI. will follow up with a small support playbook that references this doc.
